TikTok reports a profile view only for creators of 5,000 followers or fewer, so nobody is told about the visit. Never point it at a person's profile.

name: Allow Duet and Stitch

checks.what: With the switch on, no video reports a 'friends only' duet or stitch setting (value 1) and every creator-level setting reads 0, across eight videos.
The patch registered its switch.

notes: TikTok decides the duet and stitch buttons from three values (the video's setting, the creator's setting, the permission block); the patch answers the first two. The probe's videoinfo prints them through the same getters, so the on state hides every 1. The converse (finding a friends-only video with the switch off, then seeing it open with the switch on) depends on a creator who closed it; swiping eight videos usually finds none, so the check proves only that nothing closed gets through, and the owed natural check is a known friends-only video: duetSetting=1 with the switch off, 0 with it on, and the Duet button present. Setting 2 (music or partnership) is left alone on purpose. Actually making a duet is never done here.

Comment sheet with the switch on: a photo or gallery button sits in the input row. Failing looks like the same row as the off shot. Do not type or send anything.

Natural check: PineDrama, switch on, restart, open a drama's comments and tap the box: the gallery icon sits beside the emoji and @ icons; off it doesn't.

name: Block P2P video relay

checks.what: The build details baked into the APK say the P2P strip was selected and ran (stripped, already empty, or absent from a split bundle).
TikTok started and sits on the For You feed with the patch built in.

notes: The strip empties lib/arm64-v8a/libavmdlp2pv2.so and libp2plivevdp.so (and the armeabi-v7a twins). The profile for the merged split bundle of 47.1.4 lists no relay library at all ("The split bundle ships no relay library", ResourceOptimizerPatches.kt p2pRelayProfiles), so on a bundle build the record says "absent" and there is no zero-length entry to test, which is why this entry has no apk entry-empty step. If the audit APK is the universal APK, add apk entry-empty on those two arm64 paths. The record is read through the diagnostic export ([BUILD DETAILS] section of the probe "report" answer). The user-visible effect (videos handed on to other viewers) is not observable; the runtime check is that TikTok still reaches the feed.

name: Block contact list access

checks.what: SettingsStatus.contactListBlockerEnabled is true, so the patch is in this APK and the extension loaded it.

The blocker TikTok's rewired contact queries go through answers the contacts provider with an empty cursor and logs it while the switch is on, and passes the query to the provider when it's off. TikTok reads contacts on its own schedule, so the check calls that entry point with the arguments those call sites pass.

steps.log: Contact list blocker: blocked a query to \[url omitted\]

checks.what: The blocker only refuses the contacts authority: with the switch on, a media store query through the same entry point reaches the provider (its own cursor, or a SecurityException without a media permission, never the blocker's empty MatrixCursor) and nothing is logged as blocked.

notes: The 2026-09-17 device audit saw the contact blocker fire when the Friends tab opened. On TikTok 47.1.4 (2026-10-16) the Friends tab showed "From your contacts" cards matched on TikTok's server and made no local read in 15 seconds, so the check now turns the switch on before a restart and reads the log from the restart's marker (fromStep), which counts a read at start-up as well as one on Friends. On 47.5.3 (2026-10-23) Android's app-op record on the S22 showed one contacts read, at 09:15:55Z, while Hide inbox items' conversation-rows check had TikTok freshly restarted on the Inbox, and none during this check, then none in a rerun that opened Friends and the Inbox after a restart. TikTok syncs contacts on its own clock, so the check opens both and stays inconclusive between syncs. A process that never reads the contacts provider is inconclusive, not a failure: the patch log's intercepted site count is then the proof. Never open Find friends or a contacts page to force a read, since that's where TikTok asks to upload them. The log line is Logger.printInfo, which logs only with morphe_debug on (the runner turns it on for the run), and the logger replaces every URL with [url omitted], so the line can't name the authority: lets-media-queries-through reads the cursor type of a media query instead (2026-10-28). On 47.5.3 'blocks-contacts-query' read inconclusive twice (2026-10-23, S22): TikTok made its one contacts read of the session outside the check, as above.

The blocker TikTok's rewired app-list calls go through answers the package list, the application list and the launcher enumeration empty while the switch is on, and still finds the share targets the share sheet needs. With it off the same calls see the phone's apps. TikTok scans on its own schedule, so the check calls those entry points with the arguments the call sites pass.

steps.expect: ^ok privacy-call apps packages=0 applications=0 launcher=0 share=[1-9]\d*$

steps.log: Installed apps blocker: blocked the launcher enumeration

steps.expect: ^ok privacy-call apps packages=[1-9]\d* applications=[1-9]\d* launcher=[1-9]\d* share=[1-9]\d*$

notes: Reads the export (probe report) instead of logcat because TikTok scans at start-up, before the runner's log marker. The scan happens only when TikTok asks (ad SDKs, app-link checks), so the check also opens the own profile, and a session that still lists nothing reads inconclusive (the patch log's intercepted site count is the proof then, 2026-10-16). The description says opening another app from TikTok still works: that is not exercised (the runner cannot leave TikTok). Logged at Logger.printInfo, buffered by LogBufferManager.appendEvent. On 47.5.3 (2026-10-23, S22) 'blocks-package-listing' read inconclusive: the report's blocked lines stayed empty after the profile visit, so TikTok listed no packages that session.

name: Block suggested video notifications

checks.what: The patched dex routes TikTok's NotificationManager.notify calls through the blocker and carries the channel prefix it compares, and the patch registered itself. checks.what: The patched dex carries the sticker creator and the share sheet's Make sticker, and the patch registered itself. (The dex-string steps show the extension classes are shipped; the registered-switch step is what shows the patch ran and wrote the bridges.)

notes: Issues #156 and #88. The Saved page of the comment sticker panel gets a red Create pill level with its Saved heading. Tapping it opens the photo picker; the photo is shrunk to 512 px on its longest side, uploaded to ImageX with the token im/upload_config hands the comment sticker uploader (scene 2), saved through StickerApiV2's im/sticker/save as type 9 and added to the sticker store, so it shows in Saved without a reload. name: In-app browser privacy guard

settings.row: Protect external pages in TikTok's browser

checks.what: SettingsStatus.browserPrivacyGuardEnabled is true, so the patch is in this APK and the extension loaded it.

With the switch on, an external link (example.com through PineDrama's webview deep link) never loads in a PineDrama WebView: PineDrama hands its link-safety page to Chrome, and no PineDrama WebView is left to carry a bridge.

With the switch off, the same link goes the same way (PineDrama hands the link-safety page to Chrome) and the guard withholds nothing, so the switch changes no route: in PineDrama the external page never reaches a WebView that could hold a bridge.

steps.logNot: Browser privacy guard: JavaScript bridge withheld

notes: PineDrama 47.5.3 (S22, 2026-10-28): snssdk845221://webview?url=<example.com> starts DramaDeepLinkActivityV2, CrossPlatformActivity and SparkActivity, then hands https://www.tiktoklinksafety.us/... to Chrome (IntentDispatcher, then CustomTabActivity), so no PineDrama WebView loads an external page on this route and the bridge checks TikTok runs have nothing to measure. The Custom Tab becomes the root of PineDrama's task and survives a force-stop, so every later restart resumed it until BACK closed it; both checks press BACK before any step that can fail. The guard logs only when it changes a WebView's bridge state (BrowserPrivacyGuard.prepareForPage), so a trusted tiktok.com page proves nothing: the bridges stay as they are and no line appears. TikTok 47.1.4 opens an external address passed to snssdk1233://webview?url=<encoded page> (DeepLinkActivityV2) on its link-safety interstitial, www.tiktoklinksafety.us/link/ ("This link may be unsafe"), in SparkActivity, and that host is deliberately outside the trusted list, so example.com gives an untrusted page without tapping anything (discovery 8, 2026-10-16). Open external links directly is set off so the page stays in TikTok's browser. The probe's webview-bridges answers asynchronously with "bridge-exposure webview=N origin=... tracked=T java=J exposed=...": tracked is how many bridge names the guard holds for that WebView, and java is how many of them reach their Java object (a name counts when one of its @JavascriptInterface methods resolves as a function). exposed alone misleads: TikTok's JS SDK defines its own window.ToutiaoJSBridge (members _handleMessageFromApp and _handleMessageFromToutiao), which shows up even while the Java object is withheld. bridges-left-alone is the control with the switch off. The guard's "withheld" line is read from the open step on, since the probe step moves the log marker.

A phone with its animation scales at 0 (the S22's baseline) slides nothing, so the check turns them on first with an animations step and the runner puts the phone's values back afterwards; with them at 0 the switch-off half found no frames in between (2026-10-16).
